reported.title: No debounce and wrong edge polarity cause multiple toggles per press
reported.description: The loop has no settle/debounce logic at all: it reads D2 every iteration (line 52) and calls flipLed() on every risingEdge() (lines 54-57), where risingEdge() is defined as LOW->HIGH (line 28). Since the key is active LOW, the toggle fires on release rather than press, and contact bounce on both press and release produces many LOW->HIGH transitions, so measured toggle counts per press were [2,2,3,...] and [3,3,3,3] and [4], with extra toggles at 952 ms, 1.40 s and 2.00 s that no press explains. The required 40 ms settle window before accepting a press edge is never implemented. 15 of 15 press(es) did not toggle D13 exactly once; toggle counts per press were [2, 2, 3, 2, 2, 3, 3, 2, 2, 3, 2, 3, 2, 3, 2]. D13 also toggled 9 time(s) with no press to explain it, first at 952 ms.

judge_input.spec:
- Panel key on D2 to ground with internal pull-up (active LOW); status LED on D13.
- Each settled press toggles D13 exactly once within 150 ms; release must not toggle.
- Bounce up to 20 ms on press and release must not produce extra toggles.
- Use a 40 ms settle window before accepting a press edge (HIGH-to-LOW after settle).
- Print `panel led=<0|1> edges=<n>` every 1000 ms.
- Idle (unpressed) key reads HIGH.
